newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PM'S DEPUTY SEEKS REVIEW OF PARTY POLICY.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PM'S DEPUTY SEEKS REVIEW OF PARTY POLICY.

text.p: Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec, number two man in the ruling Czech Civic Democratic Party (ODS), said his party needs to answer an apparent split in the electorate growing against it.
"We have to answer the question: Is not the border beween voters of ODS and its non-voters too sharp?" Zieleniec said in an interview for a daily Lidove Noviny published on Thursday.
The party, led by the vigorously-confident Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, took 32 of 81 seats after late November runoff elections to the new upper house of Czech parliament.
But after the first round vote a week before, the ODS had the potential to win as many 79 seats.

Ahead of second round of voting, not only did opposition parties campaign against the ruling party, but ODS's centrist junior coalition partner, the Christian Democrats, backed candidates running against ODS in some constituencies.

Zieleniec, in the interview published a day before the ODS's annual national congress which will vote on the party's chairman and four vice-charimen begins, said the joint opposition growing against the ODS has to be taken seriously.

"Why it was so easy to create a unified front against the ODS in the second round (of Senate elections)? ... These are things that must be considered if we want ODS to remain the big player on the right wing," he said.
The ODS, a party in which Klaus often tries to emulate the style of former British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher, has been in control of Czech politics since winning general elections in 1992.

But Klaus and his coalition lost its majority in parliament in June lower house elections after the left-wing opposition consolidated, putting the centre-left Social Democrats in a strong second-place position.
Klaus is the only candidate on the ballot for party chairman at the ODS congress to be held on Friday and Saturday in the Czech second city Brno.

In a widely-read local newspaper interview in the summer, Zieleniec appealed for more voices to be heard in ODS. In a thinly-veiled reference to Klaus, Zieleniec implied party leadership was too autocratic.
